slot.brief: Given K for a reaction, find K for the reversed reaction and/or reaction multiplied by 2 (manipulating K).

stem: The equilibrium constant for the reaction $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2(g)$ is $K_c = 0.2$ at a certain temperature. What is the value of $K_c$ for the reaction $4\text{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$ at the same temperature?

verdicts.working: Reversing the reaction gives K' = 1/Kc = 1/0.2 = 5. Doubling the coefficients squares it: K'' = 5^2 = 25.

working:
For the given initial reaction:
$$\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2(g), \quad K_c = \dfrac{[\text{NO}_2]^2}{[\text{N}_2\text{O}_4]} = 0.2$$

Reversing the reaction gives:
$$2\text{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g), \quad K_c' = \dfrac{1}{K_c} = \dfrac{1}{0.2} = 5$$

Multiplying the reversed reaction by a factor of $2$ gives:
$$4\text{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g), \quad K_c'' = (K_c')^2 = 5^2 = 25$$

Independent check: Reversing the reaction gives K' = 1/Kc = 1/0.2 = 5. Doubling the coefficients squares it: K'' = 5^2 = 25.

draft.distractor_notes:
$0.04$ comes from squaring $K_c$ for doubling the coefficients but forgetting to invert it for reversing the reaction ($(0.2)^2 = 0.04$).
$5$ comes from inverting $K_c$ for reversing the reaction but forgetting to square it for the factor of $2$ ($1/0.2 = 5$).
$10$ comes from inverting $K_c$ and erroneously multiplying by $2$ instead of raising to the power of $2$ ($2 \times 5 = 10$).
